name: Power BI Model & DAX
env: Power BI Desktop — build this alongside the app. DAX doesn't run in-browser, so these tickets are self-checked; the app holds the briefs, the exact DAX, and the acceptance criteria.
goal: Stand the gold-layer star up inside Power BI — clean relationships, a proper date table, and a measure library a dashboard can be built from.

brief.body: I can't keep pinging you for numbers. I need a Power BI model where I can click a category or a quarter and the numbers just update — net revenue, margin, return rate, growth. Build it on the clean model Priya had you make, not the raw tables. And please make the measures right the first time — last time someone's 'revenue' double-counted because of a bad relationship.

clinic.title: From star schema to semantic model
clinic.body: Power BI loves a star: import the dim_*/fact_* views, join each dimension to the fact one-to-many with a single filter direction (dimension filters fact, not the reverse), and mark dim_date as the official date table. Then write measures (evaluated in filter context) — not calculated columns — for anything that aggregates. CALCULATE is the engine: it changes the filter context a measure runs in. Get the model right and the DAX stays short. Connection: in this app the gold layer is DuckDB views; on the job you'd Get Data → Azure Databricks, pick main → shopnow, and load the dim_*/fact_* views in Import mode.

classwork.title: Build the model — together (in Power BI Desktop)

steps.instr: Connect & load the gold views (Import mode). In Navigator tick dim_customer, dim_product, dim_date, dim_payment, dim_event, fact_sales (+ fact_web_events, marketing_spend if built).
steps.sql:
Get Data → Azure Databricks → Server Hostname + HTTP Path → sign in →
Navigator → main → shopnow → tick the dim_* / fact_* views → Load (Import).
steps.checkpoint: All selected tables appear in the Fields pane with correct row counts. No transforms needed — the gold layer is already clean.

steps.instr: Set types & mark the date table.
steps.sql:
Model/Power Query: DateKey = Date, Revenue/Profit = Decimal, keys = Text.
Table tools → Mark as date table → dim_date[DateKey].
steps.checkpoint: dim_date shows the calendar icon. Time intelligence (YTD, MoM) now works.

steps.instr: Build relationships — one-to-many, single filter direction (dimension → fact). This is the part people get wrong.
steps.sql:
dim_customer[CustomerKey] 1 --- * fact_sales[CustomerKey]
dim_product [ProductKey]  1 --- * fact_sales[ProductKey]
dim_date    [DateKey]     1 --- * fact_sales[DateKey]
-- fact_web_events reuses dim_customer / dim_product / dim_date (conformed)
steps.checkpoint: A clean star in Model view, all arrows into the fact. No two-way filters (double-counting). No relationship between two dimensions.

steps.instr: Write the base measure library (measures, not calculated columns).
steps.sql:
Total Revenue   = SUM ( fact_sales[Revenue] )
Net Revenue     = SUM ( fact_sales[NetRevenue] )     -- returns already zeroed in gold
Total Orders    = DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_sales[OrderID] )
Returned Orders = CALCULATE ( [Total Orders], fact_sales[ReturnFlag] = "Yes" )
Return Rate %   = DIVIDE ( [Returned Orders], [Total Orders] )
Net Profit      = SUMX ( fact_sales, IF ( fact_sales[ReturnFlag]="Yes", 0, fact_sales[GrossProfit] ) )
Net Margin %    = DIVIDE ( [Net Profit], [Net Revenue] )
Distinct Customers = DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_sales[CustomerKey] )
steps.checkpoint: Drop [Net Revenue] into a card and dim_product[Category] into a table — the numbers slice by category instantly. The model works.

tickets.title: Time intelligence: MoM, YTD, running total
tickets.prompt: Add the growth measures investors expect: previous-month net revenue, MoM growth %, year-to-date, and a running total. All driven by the marked dim_date. Build these in Power BI, then self-check against the acceptance criteria and reveal the reference DAX.
acceptanceCriteria: Uses the marked date table (no string dates)
MoM growth guarded against divide-by-zero / blanks (DIVIDE)
YTD and running total both present and correct on a month visual
tickets.solution:
Net Revenue LM =
CALCULATE ( [Net Revenue], DATEADD ( dim_date[DateKey], -1, MONTH ) )

Net Revenue MoM % =
DIVIDE ( [Net Revenue] - [Net Revenue LM], [Net Revenue LM] )

Net Revenue YTD =
TOTALYTD ( [Net Revenue], dim_date[DateKey] )

Net Revenue Running =
CALCULATE ( [Net Revenue],
  FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( dim_date[DateKey] ), dim_date[DateKey] <= MAX ( dim_date[DateKey] ) ) )
tickets.modelNote: DIVIDE (not '/') gives blank instead of an error on the first month. TOTALYTD and DATEADD both require the marked date table — that's why Sprint 8 step 2 matters.

tickets.title: Marketing efficiency: spend, ROAS, CAC
tickets.prompt: Relate marketing_spend to dim_date (and a cleaned channel/category) and build Total Spend, ROAS (revenue per ₹ spent) and a rough CAC (spend per new customer). Mind the 'Home&Kitchen' vs 'Home & Kitchen' mismatch — fix it in Power Query before relating.
acceptanceCriteria: Category text standardized in Power Query so it joins to dim_product category
ROAS sliceable by channel and month
tickets.solution:
-- Power Query on marketing_spend: Replace Values 'Home&Kitchen' → 'Home & Kitchen' (or Text.Trim),
-- then relate marketing_spend[spend_date] → dim_date[DateKey].

Total Spend = SUM ( marketing_spend[spend_inr] )
ROAS = DIVIDE ( [Net Revenue], [Total Spend] )        -- revenue per rupee spent
CAC  = DIVIDE ( [Total Spend], [Distinct Customers] )  -- rough cost per customer
tickets.modelNote: ROAS here attributes all revenue to spend — a blended proxy, not last-touch attribution. Name that limitation in the debrief; that's what a senior analyst does.

tickets.title: New vs returning customers & % of total
tickets.prompt: Two senior DAX patterns: a measure that counts new customers (first-ever order falls in the visual's period) and a % of Total Revenue measure that ignores the category filter for the denominator.
acceptanceCriteria: New Customers correct as you slice by month
One sentence on the filter-context reasoning
tickets.solution:
New Customers =
VAR PeriodDates = VALUES ( dim_date[DateKey] )
RETURN
COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( VALUES ( fact_sales[CustomerKey] ),
  VAR FirstOrder = CALCULATE ( MIN ( fact_sales[DateKey] ), ALLEXCEPT ( fact_sales, fact_sales[CustomerKey] ) )
  RETURN FirstOrder IN PeriodDates ) )

% of Total Revenue =
DIVIDE ( [Net Revenue], CALCULATE ( [Net Revenue], ALLSELECTED ( dim_product ) ) )
tickets.modelNote: New Customers re-computes each customer's first-ever order date ignoring the date filter (ALLEXCEPT), then keeps only those whose first order lands in the visible period. % of Total strips the product filter from the denominator with ALLSELECTED so each category shows its share of the visible total.
